description: Verify that DUT's ARP Reply carries its own iface MAC as the Ethernet source — peer-side validation must trust eth_src to match sender_mac (RFC 826 §2.4)
approach:
[Objective]
Field-level breakdown of the Reply emitted in ARP_41. eth_src on a unicast Reply is the responder's iface MAC — it must equal sender_mac (the answer to the Request) for stack-level integrity.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: ARP Request (target_ip=DUT IP)

2. Observation (3 s window):
   • DUT → Tester: ARP Reply
      - eth_src     == DUT iface MAC   ← key check
      - sender_mac  == DUT iface MAC
      - opcode      == 2

[Pass condition]
The Reply's eth_src equals DUT iface MAC.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_eth_src_not_dut_mac — Reply was emitted but eth_src differed from iface MAC (bridge/bond rewrite suspected)
• Fail_no_reply — DUT did not respond at all

verdicts.Pass: Reply eth_src matched DUT iface MAC — normal
verdicts.Fail_eth_src_not_dut_mac: Reply emitted but eth_src ≠ iface MAC (bridge/bond rewrite?)
verdicts.Fail_no_reply: DUT did not respond to the Request
